chapter_title: Concerning the Seven Works of the Living Spirit
chapter_note: An exceptionally clean substrate chapter. A seven-fold enumeration of the Living Spirit's cosmic works — rescue, binding, construction, distribution — with both sides of every mapping staying within the cosmic system. Teaching purity is 1.000 with zero editorial fatigue. The only non-substrate material is the dialogue frame formula in ¶1 and the beatitude closure in ¶10. Paragraph 9 adds a supplementary eschatological work (the Last Statue) beyond the numbered seven, but its content remains entirely cosmological. Heavy lacunae in ¶7-9 but the teaching structure is preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: The Living Spirit has done seven [wo]rks with his strength.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame formula '[Once] again the enlightener speaks:' — standard editorial attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The frame formula is late editorial attribution. The substantive statement defines the teaching structure (seven works) and belongs to the oldest layer.

paragraphs.core_text: [The fi]rst: He brought the First Man up from the contest, the way a pearl is [brought] up from the sea.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First enumeration unit. The pearl-from-sea simile is correspondential — pearl maps to First Man, sea maps to the contest/abyss. Both sides stay within the cosmic system. The pearl image is deeply archaic in the correspondential tradition.

paragraphs.core_text: [The second: He spread about the one who had rebelled, he crucified [h]im in every body.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second enumeration unit. 'The one who had rebelled' is the cosmic rebel (Darkness/archons). 'Crucified him in every body' describes the binding of dark substance into material forms — cosmic process, not Christological reference. Both sides within cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: The third: He [tr]ampled, piled up, and pierced the essences of death.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Third enumeration unit. 'Essences of death' — cosmic dark substance. Three verbs (trampled, piled up, pierced) describe the cosmic act of subjugating dark matter for universe-construction.

paragraphs.core_text: [The f]ourth: He constructed the ships of light.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fourth enumeration unit. 'Ships of light' = sun and moon as cosmic vessels. Terse, systematic, impersonal.

paragraphs.core_text: The fi[f]th: He evoked his five sons, and distributed them about. They [took] possession of the zone, they bore up under all the universe's weight. Also, he evoked three living words. He set [them] upon the th[re]e vessels, another one upon the giant. [Again, he evoked the] summons, that it might be mixed with the five shining men.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fifth enumeration unit — the longest and most detailed. Dense with cosmic entities: five sons, zone, three living words, three vessels, the giant, the summons, five shining men. 'Evoked' (emanation verb) appears three times. The five-fold structure and emanation hierarchy are hallmarks of the oldest teaching layer. Substrate score 29.31 confirms heavy cosmological vocabulary.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.86⟩ The sixth: When he had constructed the zone he aro[se] and s[e]nt forth a multitude of powers and many [angel]s; so that they would bound the circuit of the z[o]ne on every si[de], un[t]il he finished [co]nstructing the works. And at the end [of] all the [wor]ks he to[ok s]ome of them into his storehouses, and he appointed others at the watch-posts.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Sixth enumeration unit. Zone construction, circuit-binding, storehouses, watch-posts — all cosmic architectural terms. The process is systematic: construct → send powers → bound circuit → finish → distribute to storehouses and watch-posts. Both sides of every mapping stay within cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: The [sev]enth: A[t the] time when the Ambass[ador dis]pl[aye]d his glorious imag[e], the L[iving] Spirit [established] many [go]ds and angels. They [ ... ] Th[ey to]ok hold of it, that the entire building [ ... ] not [ ... / ... ] one another against [the] light, which he had [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Seventh enumeration unit, heavily damaged by lacunae. The Ambassador, his image-display, the Living Spirit establishing gods and angels, 'the entire building' — all cosmic architecture. Despite the damage, the teaching structure (enumeration marker + cosmic process) is clearly preserved.

paragraphs.core_text: Also another gr[ea]t and glorious work he will enact at the e[nd] is [the] Last [Statue], which he will bring up to the aeons of [light]; and he [ ... ] in, and [he ta]kes hold, and he smites [ ... ], and [he] builds, and he [ ... ], and he [ ... t]hem.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Supplementary work beyond the numbered seven. 'Also another' marks it as addendum, but the content is entirely cosmological: the Last Statue, the aeons of light. The Last Statue is the eschatological gathering of all light — cosmic process, not institutional application. No editorial bridge vocabulary. Heavily damaged but structurally intact as cosmic teaching.

Classic beatitude closure: 'Blessed is he who knows him in the new aeon.' The 'Blessed is he who...' formula is a standard devotional wrapper appended to substrate teaching. Shifts from impersonal cosmic description to direct address about eschatological reward ('glory and joy'). Positioned at chapter end — classic exhortation placement.
